name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Check that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: semantic-crosscheck generates a PostgreSQL hierarchy closure, SQL and SHACL data rules, an OWL ontology and a Cube data model from one crosscheck.toml and checks on your data that they agree with each other and with hand-written gold SQL. A pass means the checks that ran found no disagreement; it is not proof that the model or the business rules are right, and the not_proven lines list what was not shown. Since v0.22.0 there is an optional data-rules stage: typed rules from a separate rule file are evaluated twice on one read-only PostgreSQL snapshot, as compiled SQL with bound parameters and as an independent standard-library Python evaluation, and a rule gets a verdict only when both agree and its authored examples hold. With views enabled, build creates lookup views whose rows data-rules certifies, so the keys a rule found are read in the database while results keep counts and ids only. Unsupported types, nondeterministic collations, NaN, NULL or duplicate keys, cycles and row budgets leave rules not_run, never passed. Configurations without data_rules keep byte-identical build output, results and reports apart from the engine fingerprint, and report never reads the data-rules result. Agreement of the two evaluations is not proof of the business rule. Earlier contract/plan report evidence, SQL structure diagnostics and synthetic fixtures are unchanged. Since v0.23.0 every check counts under an evidence kind (authored gold SQL, an independent recomputation, generated layers, structural, mutation), and a passing V4 mutant check records whether a replayed authored gold query or only a check between generated layers detected the change; facets of measures and hierarchies without authored evidence and gold queries that compared no row are named in not_proven lines and in the report; statuses change only in the opt-in require mode, and V4 statuses also when a gold query contains generated text. Rerun operational stages after upgrading because engine code changed. Publication does not update active installations or company databases.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
